chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Adam ibn Ali, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever performs Hajj on behalf of a person who does not have the wealth to perform Hajj with, it suffices for him until God grants him the means to perform Hajj and it becomes obligatory upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs Hajj on behalf of a person who cannot afford it yet?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the mechanism of Hajj al-Badal (substitute Hajj) for those who are financially unable but not permanently exempt, establishing that the obligation remains suspended until divine provision allows for personal performance. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between temporary inability, where a proxy's Hajj suffices, and permanent inability, which may require a different ruling, ensuring the debt of Hajj is cleared without double obligation.
